<reason>Both sides argued the motion as written and converged on proportionality, so the debate turned on whether "distinct from traditional GMO regulation" adds anything beyond a technique-shaped label. CON built and sustained the cleaner comparative: a unified product-based tiering framework that delivers every proportionality gain PRO wants while removing the gaming boundary, plus the asymmetry that edited products are precisely the ones no port assay, recall, or shopper can identify later — so the pre-market check is the only check and should not be the light one. CON's pressure questions did real damage: forcing PRO to name a concrete eligibility criterion extracted the concession that the eligible case is an allele already in the gene pool (so the lane buys crossing speed, not new capability, while the disease-resistance and drought benefits from PRO's opening fall into full assessment), and forcing the port-test question extracted "a rejected shipment can indeed hurt the farmer." Those two concessions hollowed PRO's benefit story while CON's costs stayed live. PRO did land a genuine hit — the symmetry turn that CON's own risk tiers require the same evidence-based screening PRO uses, which dissolved CON's "rigorous gate means nothing is streamlined" dilemma, and the fair point that keeping GMO rules does not make breeding history detectable. PRO also had a real feasibility edge (act now on a defined subset rather than reopen all breeding oversight) that CON only waved off as expedience, but PRO never weighed it hard enough to outrank CON's entrenchment-and-undetectability package. CON's opening and closing were both clipped for length, a real execution cost that cost it the final crystallizing sentence; that keeps the margin from widening.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's [B4.4]: once PRO's eligibility test narrowed to edits recreating an allele already cultivated and eaten, CON showed conventional crossing can already deliver that allele, so the streamlined lane buys speed rather than capability — while PRO's headline benefits (disease resistance, drought tolerance) are novel traits routed to full assessment. Paired with "PRO's safe pathway is nearly empty; PRO's useful pathway is the one my potato and cassava cases break," this squeezed PRO's benefit down to breeder convenience, and PRO's closing effectively accepted it.</best_rebuttal>
